comment.narrative: 11 out of 17 counties submitted results totaling 14,658 households, thus 57,166. Despite these submissions, none of the counties passed verification at the desk review stage and consequently field/physical verification was not conducted for DLI 2 submissions. title.narrative: People provided with sustainable access to improved sanitation services (disaggregated by gender, refugees, and host community members)

comment.narrative: Indicator generates data from DLI 4 where 8,958 households were reported from 8 counties translating to 34,936 individuals using an average of 3.9 persons per household. Due to the 80 percent rule, only 1 of the 19 counties (Kirinyaga), passed verification, where 275 households met the threshold with a 91.6% pass rate, the total disbursement under DLI 4 was US$8,250, against a potential of US$269,000 if all submissions had passed. 11 counties did not submit results pointing to the need for sustained TA in implementing CLTS methodologies; harmonization of K-WASH data with the Ministry of Health's reporting systems and intensified capacity-building on sanitation marketing approaches required. There is need to ensure increased pass rates for verification through increased TA to Counties. The next PRMR template should have a disaggregation should include a disaggregation of the households by gender.

title.narrative: Villages that achieve and sustain open defecation free (ODF) status

comment.narrative:
Results are under verification. The process is expected to be completed by mid November 2025.
ODF status requires: (a) no exposed human excreta within the community/households; (b) all households have access to a toilet (individual or shared); (c) the squat hole is covered; (d) the floor is free of faeces and urine; (e) there is a super structure that provides privacy; and (f) all households have a hand washing facility near the latrine with soap/ash and water.

title.narrative: Villages that achieve and sustain open defecation free (ODF) status

comment.narrative: A total of 1,228 villages were submitted as having achieved ODF status. Strong CLTS adoption was noted although there was uneven county performance pointing to the need for renewed technical assistance in implementing CLTS methodologies. Unfortunately, only 21 villages in Kitui County (of the 1,228 villages) passed verification therefore the verification integrity requires strengthening.

title.narrative: Amount of financing leveraged by WSPs from private/commercial financing sources

comment.narrative: While there were no results reported in Year 1, a pipeline of US$4M is expected in FY26 against a targeted US$1million. The first two WSPs are on track to sign loan agreements totaling US$4M by April 30, 2026, with the remaining agreements expected to be finalized by December 2026. It is expected that additional disbursements may be made within FY 2025/26 for the 2 WSPs.

title.narrative: WSPs that are fully compliant with the legal and regulatory requirements

comment.narrative: This indicator draws data from DLI 6. 14 WSPs passed DLI 6 requirements in year 1 and are to receive disbursements. Another 13 WSPS are likely to achieve this DLI by 30th June 2026 with a first tranche of 6 expected to qualify by 30th April 2026. PIAP operationalization is needed.

title.narrative: WSPs with at least 1/3 share of women in leadership positions

comment.narrative: This measures the percentage or women from the total personnel in those positions. Eligible positions include: technical (medium and high skilled), b) management and c) other leadership (such as Board of Director) positions. The % of women in these positions are tracked for each WSP. The % of WSPs with at least 1/3 women in such positions is reported.

title.narrative: WSP customers satisfied with their water supply services

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the number of WSPs that measure at least 80% satisfaction in customers supplied by WSPs under the Program in the areas of: continuity and reliability of supply, water quality and cost. Monitoring includes metadata on the nature of service problems, time to resolution, and other elements as defined in the County-WSP contract.
